title: Cross-service trace-handoff and anomaly triage orchestration
creator: Aisha Gomez
description:
Problem: Our current tracing pipeline fragments spans across sdk-side buffering, gateway proxies, and the inference runtime. During multi-hop requests (hosted API -> dedicated proxy -> runtime shard) the handoff between agents often drops contextual tags (customer_id, route_id, model_variant), which reduces the fidelity of SLO attribution and makes anomaly triage slow. Additionally, the alerting system sees token-latency spikes as isolated incidents rather than correlated burn-rate events across routes.

Goal: Build a lightweight trace-handoff shim plus enrichment layer that stitches spans deterministically across process boundaries and emits a compact triage envelope for the alerting pipeline. This ticket covers the runtime + gateway changes, metric/log pipeline adjustments, dashboard definitions, and the initial burn-rate anomaly scoring integration.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic span-handoff implemented: span IDs and primary tags (customer_id, route, model_variant, request_sequence_id) persist across proxy and runtime handoffs in >= 99.9% of synthetic multi-hop requests
Triage envelope produced for each request path and available in the alerting Kafka topic (observability.triage.envelopes) with contract v1
Burn-rate service can consume triage envelopes and attribute anomalies to route+model_variant with <10s end-to-end latency
New latency/error dashboards show grouped per-route burn-rate and a time-series of upstream hop failure attribution
On-call runbook updated with triage workflow and runbook links (playbook includes automated playbook hints produced by the anomaly scorer)
work_items: Design span-handoff contract and fail-open semantics (ENG PRD: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Span+Handoff+Design)
Implement lightweight transitive header (X-RW-TraceCtx) in gateway and runtime sidecar
Span-stitcher library (Go/Python) for deterministic parent-child re-linking
Add enrichment step in consumer pipeline to merge logs/metrics with triage envelopes
Extend alerting ingestion to accept triage envelopes and produce burn-rate group signals
Create dashboard: 'Triaged Burn Rate — Routes' and add widgets for model_variant heatmap
Author runbook and test playbooks using synthetic probes
decisions: Use a minimal header-based handoff (X-RW-TraceCtx) instead of full OTLP streaming to reduce ops surface and preserve upstream privacy boundaries
Fail-open: if handoff header missing, runtime will continue serving but tag spans with 'handoff:missing' for post-hoc grouping
Triage envelope schema v1 will be compact (<=1KB) and publish to Kafka topic observability.triage.envelopes; payload is base64-encoded JSON to keep brokers agnostic
Anomaly scoring will initially be statistical (z-score over rolling-window) and later replaced by ML model if needed
risks: Header propagation may be stripped by customer proxies or intermediate CDNs—mitigation: detect and surface 'propagation_lost' signal and fall back to sampling-based attribution
Additional latency from enrichment step could affect SLOs if not batched correctly—mitigation: asynchronous enrichment and backpressure caps
Kafka schema churn risk—mitigation: support dual-readers and schema-compatibility checks during rollout
implementation_notes: Prototype used a short 128-bit handoff token (tracectx) derived from upstream span id + random nonce to avoid leaking customer ids in headers
Span-stitcher will attempt three re-link strategies: header-based relink, sampling trace correlation, and eventual log-merge by request_sequence_id
Metric enrichment will join on request_sequence_id using the new deterministic hash to avoid heavy cardinality on metrics backends
Burn-rate ingestion will pre-aggregate per-tenant per-route counts to reduce downstream cardinality before scoring
dashboard_definitions: Triaged Burn Rate — Routes: primary graph = burn-rate over 1m/5m/15m windows; secondary = error share by upstream hop
Model Variant Heatmap: rows=model_variant, cols=time buckets, value=relative burn-rate deviation
Trace Handoff Loss Rate: percent of requests where 'propagation_lost' or 'handoff:missing' flagged
testing_plan: End-to-end synthetic suite that drives multi-hop requests with controlled latencies and error injections
Chaos test: strip headers at random intermediary to verify 'propagation_lost' detection and downstream attribution
Load test: validate triage envelope throughput at 5x expected peak and ensure Kafka lag stays <30s
rollout_plan: Canary: enable header injection for 2% of traffic on staging and 0.5% on prod for 24h
Observe trace-handoff loss and burn-rate signal stability; if loss >0.5% after 24h, abort
Increase to 10% then 50% then full rollout with 24h observation windows
If downstream Kafka lags increase >2x, pause enrichment and backfill triage envelopes asynchronously
runbook_updates: Added section: 'Triaged burn-rate incident' with steps to query triage envelopes, rebuild sequence, and identify upstream hop causing errors
Automated playbook link added to pager notification with quick links to top 5 affected routes
